data.name: My Vet Practice – Marine Patrol
data.detailed_description:
Características

  • Enjoy an exciting mix of animal care, practice creation and environmental protection in Canada
  • Help popular coastal and marine critters such as dolphins, baby polar bears, penguins, sea lions, orcas...
  • Discover the massive 3D scenario including Rescue Centre, beach, ocean and islands
  • Experience spectacular rescue missions with your speedboat near floes or remote islands
  • Face the duties of a real vet, including diagnosis, treatment and challenging mini games: making x-rays, cleaning wounds, administering injections, petting, feeding, cleaning…
  • Think green: collect waste, clean oil-covered animals...


Acerca do jogo

Your very own vet practice at the ocean! In the north of Canada the most popular creatures of the coast and sea need your help. Along with other young vets you follow the lead of a renowned professor at the Rescue Centre and take care of different animals in the Rescue Centre, at the beach, on floes or the neighbouring islands: Dolphins, Baby Polar Bears, Penguins, Sea Lions, Puffins, Seagulls and even Orcas. The more animals you treat during a single day the fast you can expand the Rescue Centre to admit larger and larger patients.

In many different mini games you have to tackle the challenges of a real vet, from diagnostics to treatments and care by petting. It's also part of your job to feed the animals and clean their compounds. That way everysingle patient will be fine again in no time!

Take your own speedboat to help animals in the open sea or explore neighbouring islands. And, of course, the protecting the environment is important to help animals in the ocean and at the beach. Clean up litter and help animals covered in oil.

Experience all the daily challenges of a veterinarian!

reviews.review:
My Vet Practice - Marine Patrol is slightly better than the first game in the series. Although that's kind of like saying that 10 fire ant bites are better than 100.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YJPVt4epBdc

In the game you play as a vet that needs to take care of injured wildlife in Northern Canada. This boils down to completing some simple mini-games to treat the animals and set them back free in the wild.

It's about as simple and boring as you could imagine. Park Rangers bring in the same animals constantly and many of the tactics used to treat animals are very similar to eachother. Usually you end up clicking and dragging the mouse around a certain part of the animal.

The minigames are actually improved upon from the original though. In the first game you would haphazardly fiddle with different tools until you figured out what to do, while this one just gives you them to make it easier and quicker. I appreciate that aspect because I didn't smack my head on my desk quite as quickly.

The game moves at a very slow pace where after nearly an hour I was still treating gulls and puffins even though the game said I would be treating larger animals and had purchased the dock to do so.

There are quite a few spelling mistakes in the dialogue and it repeats very often.

The game also isn't accurate to the region of the world it takes place in. As I said the game is set in Canada yet there are penguins and dolphins, neither of which live in the Arctic Circle. Penguins in particular literally live on the opposite side of the world. I wouldn't have a problem with it if the game didn't specify where it was set, but it's detailed as Canada in the description which simply doesn't make sense.

At one point the game was most likely a Nintendo DS title called Pet Vet: Marine Patrol. This is evident as the title screen for the game on startup still uses that as the title. It seems like Anikids is just releasing ports of their DS games and changing their names so nobody would see the reviews for the portable versions. That's not really an okay thing to do, Anikids.

While this is probably the best Anikids developed or published game I've played (the others are truly awful), it still isn't something I would give to a child to play. It's basic to the point that there is no fun to be had by anyone of any age. You can make good kids games that are enjoyable to play, even if they have simple mechanics. This is just lazy developing under the guise of being kid-friendly.

Also, I'm still convinced that Anikids is a tax writeoff as they are owned by a German editing software company. 


If you found this review helpful, feel free to follow my curator page to see everything I cover. http://steamcommunity.com/groups/iampattyjack#curation
